newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Tempered gasoline stock draw seen in APIs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Tempered gasoline stock draw seen in APIs.

text.p: A tempered draw in gasoline stocks is expected in Tuesday evening's oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) as traders are unclear whether there will be steady gasoline demand this spring.

"This report will be important in that we are waiting to see whether strong (gasoline) demand continues or not. I still believe that gasoline demand is going to grow by about one percent or so, so we should be seeing strong gasoline demand again," said Chevron Corp analyst Pat Hughes.
The oil stock data reflects the week ended April 11.
Trader estimates for gasoline stocks ranged from steady to down 2.5 million barrels.

The Energy Information Administration (EIA) has said that it expects gasoline demand to rise by 1.5 percent in 1997 or 7.97 million barrels per day (bpd), but dealers said floods in the Midwest in the past several weeks has dampened driving this spring. The API data for the last three weeks has yielded implied gasoline demand on average of 7.7 million bpd.
"The floods have really dampened demand I think, and some people are sort of forgetting about them in the forecast," said a New York dealer.
Also contributing to a murky gasoline demand picture is an erratic implied demand picture thus far for spring.
Although last week's API data put gasoline implied demand at a lofty 8.1 million bpd, dealers expect the demand figure was overstated, leading to a downward correction in this week's data.
"The data collecting it seems has been flawed, but I think on average, gasoline demand will end up rising longer term," said William Brown, president of New York trading firm W.H. Brown & Co.
Meanwhile, crude stocks are expected to rise due to the continuing strong pace of imports, with estimates calling for a build of up to 3.5 million barrels.

Unseasonably cold weather in the key heating oil region of the U.S. Northeast is expected to lead to a draw in distillate stocks of up to 2.5 million barrels. Distillate stocks are comprised of heating oil and diesel. Refinery runs are seen unchanged at 94.3 percent.
